--- title: "2 · Data" --- ::: {.cell} ::: We demonstrate SINDy using an [APSIM simulation dataset](https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/24843705) of wheat (Bustos-Korts et al., 2019). The dataset contains daily biomass trajectories of 199 genotypes in 31 years (1983 to 2013) at Narrabri (New South Wales). The trajectories are generated by APSIM, a crop growth model, and are influenced by weather conditions, which are the same for all genotypes within a year. ![The data. (a) Daily temperature range in the year 1998. (b) Biomass trajectories of the 199 genotypes in that year, with the genotypes of lowest and highest final biomass and genotype g114 in colour. (c) Genotype g114 in all 31 years, with 1998 in colour: the weather differs between years, and so does the trajectory.](images/concept_data.png){width=100%} ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} wx <- read.csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv") traj <- read.csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz") head(wx, 3) head(traj, 3) ``` ::: ## Python ```python import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import pandas as pd from dgxe import * wx = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv") traj = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz") print(wx.head(3)) print(traj.head(3)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` year das Tmin Tmax Rain RAD VP DL TT RAW 1 1983 15 10.0 17.0 0 12 11 11.191 247.50 0.7966 2 1983 16 3.5 15.0 0 11 10 11.180 256.75 0.7909 3 1983 17 6.0 15.5 0 13 10 11.169 267.50 0.7838 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` genotype year das biomass lai 1 g001 1983 15 0.0164 0.039 2 g001 1983 16 0.0190 0.043 3 g001 1983 17 0.0228 0.049 ``` ::: ::: ## Weather variables The weather table has one row per day and year, with the year (`year`), the days after sowing (`das`) and the following given variables. | Variable | Description | |---|---| | `Tmin`, `Tmax` | daily minimum and maximum temperature (°C) | | `Rain` | rainfall (mm) | | `RAD` | solar radiation (MJ m⁻² d⁻¹) | | `VP` | vapour pressure (hPa) | | `DL` | day length (h) | The table also contains two covariates that were constructed from these variables: `TT` and `RAW`. ## Constructed variables Two further variables in the table are constructed from the weather variables: thermal time (`TT`) and relative available water (`RAW`). ```{=html}
weather variables (given)
constructed variables
Tmin
Tmax
Rain
RAD
VP
DL
TT thermal time
\(\sum_{s \le t} \max\left(\tfrac{T_{\min,s} + T_{\max,s}}{2}, 0\right)\)
RAW relative available water
\(W_t / W_{\max}\), bucket of rain and \(\mathrm{ET}_0\)
``` Thermal time measures the development of the crop. It is the cumulative sum of the thermal time of each day, the mean temperature truncated at zero: $$ \mathrm{TT}_t = \sum_{s \le t} \max\left(\frac{T_{\min,s} + T_{\max,s}}{2},\, 0\right). $$ The sum starts at sowing, so `TT` on the first day in the table (day 15) already contains the first 14 days. Relative available water describes the water status of the soil. It is the filling of a soil-water bucket: rainfall $P_t$ adds water, evaporative demand removes it, and the bucket has a capacity $W_{\max}$, $$ W_t = \min\bigl(\max(W_{t-1} + P_t - k\,\mathrm{ET}_{0,t},\, 0),\, W_{\max}\bigr), \qquad \mathrm{RAW}_t = \frac{W_t}{W_{\max}}. $$ The table contains `RAW` but neither the loss term nor the capacity. We identified them from the table itself. `RAW` is the same for all genotypes, so it cannot come from the crop simulation, and on every dry day it decreases by an amount that follows radiation, temperature and humidity. The one-step change $\mathrm{RAW}_t - \mathrm{RAW}_{t-1}$ on days without clipping (4034 days) is explained by $P_t/W_{\max} - k\,\mathrm{ET}_{0,t}/W_{\max}$, where $\mathrm{ET}_0$ is the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith reference evapotranspiration (mm d⁻¹) computed from the weather variables of the table: | Water loss $\mathrm{ET}_0$ | RMSE of $\mathrm{RAW}_t - \mathrm{RAW}_{t-1}$ | |---|---| | linear in `RAD`, mean temperature and vapour pressure deficit | 0.0006 | | Hargreaves | 0.0014 | | Priestley–Taylor | 0.0015 | | FAO-56 Penman–Monteith | 0.0001 | The error of the last row is at the rounding of `RAW` (four decimals). The two constants were fitted to these one-step changes: $k = 0.796$ and $W_{\max} = 217.2$ mm. Wind is not in the table, so the FAO-56 default $u_2 = 2$ m s⁻¹ is used; fitting $u_2$ as well gives 2.04 m s⁻¹. The reference evapotranspiration is, with $T = (T_{\min} + T_{\max})/2$, $$ \mathrm{ET}_0 = \frac{0.408\,\Delta\,R_n + \gamma\,\dfrac{900}{T + 273}\,u_2\,(e_s - e_a)}{\Delta + \gamma\,(1 + 0.34\,u_2)}. $$ Its ingredients are computed from the table as follows (temperatures in °C, pressures in kPa, radiation in MJ m⁻² d⁻¹). The vapour pressure of the air is $e_a = \mathrm{VP}/10$ and the saturation vapour pressure is $e^\circ(\tau) = 0.6108\exp\bigl(17.27\,\tau/(\tau + 237.3)\bigr)$, so that $$ e_s = \frac{e^\circ(T_{\max}) + e^\circ(T_{\min})}{2}, \qquad \Delta = \frac{4098\,e^\circ(T)}{(T + 237.3)^2}, \qquad \gamma = 0.000665 \cdot 101.3\left(\frac{293 - 0.0065\,z}{293}\right)^{5.26}. $$ The net radiation is the absorbed shortwave radiation minus the outgoing longwave radiation, $$ R_n = (1 - 0.23)\,\mathrm{RAD} - R_{nl}, \qquad R_{nl} = \sigma\,\frac{(T_{\max} + 273.16)^4 + (T_{\min} + 273.16)^4}{2}\,\bigl(0.34 - 0.14\sqrt{e_a}\bigr)\left(1.35\,\min\Bigl(\frac{\mathrm{RAD}}{R_{so}}, 1\Bigr) - 0.35\right), $$ with $\sigma = 4.903\cdot 10^{-9}$ MJ K⁻⁴ m⁻² d⁻¹ and the elevation $z$ in metres. The clear-sky radiation $R_{so} = (0.75 + 2\cdot 10^{-5} z)\,R_a$ follows from the extraterrestrial radiation $R_a$, which needs only the day length `DL` and the latitude $\varphi = -30.32^\circ$ of Narrabri: with the sunset hour angle $\omega_s = \pi\,\mathrm{DL}/24$ and the solar declination $\delta$ given by $\tan\delta = -\cos\omega_s/\tan\varphi$, $$ R_a = \frac{24 \cdot 60}{\pi}\,0.0820\,\bigl(\omega_s \sin\varphi \sin\delta + \cos\varphi \cos\delta \sin\omega_s\bigr). $$ The latitude and the elevation $z = 230$ m are approximate values for Narrabri (assumed, not fitted), the albedo 0.23 is the FAO-56 value of the reference grass surface, and the Earth–Sun distance factor of $R_a$ is omitted. Starting from the given value of the first day of each year, this construction reproduces `RAW` over the whole season with an RMSE of 0.0018 (largest error 0.007, about 1.5 mm of water). The first day of the table (day 15) is not an initial condition we can reconstruct, because the weather before it is not in the table; its value is nearly the same in every year (0.80 ± 0.01). ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} reference_et <- function(wx, lat = -30.32, elev = 230, albedo = 0.23, u2 = 2) { sat <- function(T) 0.6108 * exp(17.27 * T / (T + 237.3)) Tm <- (wx$Tmin + wx$Tmax) / 2 ea <- wx$VP / 10 es <- (sat(wx$Tmax) + sat(wx$Tmin)) / 2 slope <- 4098 * sat(Tm) / (Tm + 237.3)^2 gamma <- 0.000665 * 101.3 * ((293 - 0.0065 * elev) / 293)^5.26 phi <- lat * pi / 180 ws <- wx$DL * pi / 24 dec <- atan(-cos(ws) / tan(phi)) Ra <- 24 * 60 / pi * 0.082 * (ws * sin(phi) * sin(dec) + cos(phi) * cos(dec) * sin(ws)) Rso <- (0.75 + 2e-5 * elev) * Ra Rnl <- 4.903e-9 * ((wx$Tmax + 273.16)^4 + (wx$Tmin + 273.16)^4) / 2 * (0.34 - 0.14 * sqrt(ea)) * (1.35 * pmin(wx$RAD / Rso, 1) - 0.35) Rn <- (1 - albedo) * wx$RAD - Rnl (0.408 * slope * Rn + gamma * 900 / (Tm + 273) * u2 * (es - ea)) / (slope + gamma * (1 + 0.34 * u2)) } reconstruct_raw <- function(wx, k = 0.796, Wmax = 217.2) { loss <- k * reference_et(wx) raw <- wx$RAW # each year starts from its given value for (j in seq_len(nrow(wx))[-1]) { if (wx$year[j] == wx$year[j - 1]) { raw[j] <- min(max(raw[j - 1] + (wx$Rain[j] - loss[j]) / Wmax, 0), 1) } } raw } wx <- wx[order(wx$year, wx$das), ] err <- reconstruct_raw(wx) - wx$RAW cat(sprintf("RMSE %.4f, largest %.4f\n", sqrt(mean(err^2)), max(abs(err)))) ``` ::: ## Python ```python def reference_et(wx, lat=-30.32, elev=230.0, albedo=0.23, u2=2.0): sat = lambda T: 0.6108 * np.exp(17.27 * T / (T + 237.3)) Tm = (wx.Tmin + wx.Tmax) / 2 ea = wx.VP / 10 es = (sat(wx.Tmax) + sat(wx.Tmin)) / 2 slope = 4098 * sat(Tm) / (Tm + 237.3) ** 2 gamma = 0.000665 * 101.3 * ((293 - 0.0065 * elev) / 293) ** 5.26 phi = np.radians(lat) ws = wx.DL * np.pi / 24 dec = np.arctan(-np.cos(ws) / np.tan(phi)) Ra = 24 * 60 / np.pi * 0.082 * (ws * np.sin(phi) * np.sin(dec) + np.cos(phi) * np.cos(dec) * np.sin(ws)) Rso = (0.75 + 2e-5 * elev) * Ra Rnl = (4.903e-9 * ((wx.Tmax + 273.16) ** 4 + (wx.Tmin + 273.16) ** 4) / 2 * (0.34 - 0.14 * np.sqrt(ea)) * (1.35 * np.minimum(wx.RAD / Rso, 1) - 0.35)) Rn = (1 - albedo) * wx.RAD - Rnl return ((0.408 * slope * Rn + gamma * 900 / (Tm + 273) * u2 * (es - ea)) / (slope + gamma * (1 + 0.34 * u2))) def reconstruct_raw(wx, k=0.796, Wmax=217.2): loss = (k * reference_et(wx)).to_numpy() raw = wx.RAW.to_numpy().copy() # each year starts from its given value year, rain = wx.year.to_numpy(), wx.Rain.to_numpy() for j in range(1, len(wx)): if year[j] == year[j - 1]: raw[j] = min(max(raw[j - 1] + (rain[j] - loss[j]) / Wmax, 0.0), 1.0) return raw wx = wx.sort_values(["year", "das"]) err = reconstruct_raw(wx) - wx.RAW.to_numpy() print(f"RMSE {np.sqrt((err**2).mean()):.4f}, largest {np.abs(err).max():.4f}") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` RMSE 0.0018, largest 0.0069 ``` ::: ::: In total there are eight variables: the six weather variables and the two constructed ones. All of them are candidates for the library. ## Variables over the years All eight variables, for all years (grey) and three selected years: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} vars <- c("Tmin", "Tmax", "Rain", "RAD", "VP", "DL", "TT", "RAW") w <- data.frame( year = wx$year, das = wx$das, variable = factor(rep(vars, each = nrow(wx)), vars), value = unlist(wx[vars]) ) shown <- w[w$year %in% c(1984, 1998, 2008), ] ggplot(w, aes(das, value, group = year)) + geom_line(colour = "#D1D5DB", linewidth = 0.25) + geom_line(data = shown, aes(colour = factor(year)), linewidth = 0.7) + facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) + scale_colour_dgxe("blue", "cyan", "burgundy") + labs(x = "days after sowing", y = NULL) + theme_dgxe() + legend_top() ``` ::: ## Python ```python VARS = ["Tmin", "Tmax", "Rain", "RAD", "VP", "DL", "TT", "RAW"] years = [1984, 1998, 2008] fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(10, 4.5), sharex=True) for ax, name in zip(axes.flat, VARS): for year, g in wx.groupby("year"): ax.plot(g["das"], g[name], color=GREY, lw=0.25) for year, colour in zip(years, [BLUE, CYAN, BURGUNDY]): g = wx[wx["year"] == year] ax.plot(g["das"], g[name], color=colour, lw=0.9, label=year) ax.set_title(name, loc="left") axes[0, 0].legend(frameon=False) fig.supxlabel("days after sowing") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-data_files/figure-html/02-3-run-1.png){width=1036.8} ::: ::: ## Correlation Correlation of the eight variables over all days and years: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} r <- cor(wx[vars]) long <- data.frame(a = factor(rep(vars, each = 8), vars), b = factor(rep(vars, 8), rev(vars)), r = as.vector(r)) ggplot(long, aes(a, b, fill = r)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), size = 3) + scale_fill_gradient2(low = dgxe[["burgundy"]], mid = "white", high = dgxe[["blue"]], limits = c(-1, 1)) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "correlation") + theme_dgxe() + theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), legend.position = "right") ``` ::: ## Python ```python from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap colours = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("dgxe", [BURGUNDY, "white", BLUE]) corr = wx[VARS].corr() fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4.2)) image = ax.imshow(corr, cmap=colours, vmin=-1, vmax=1) ax.set_xticks(range(8), VARS, rotation=45, ha="right") ax.set_yticks(range(8), VARS) for i in range(8): for j in range(8): ax.text(j, i, f"{corr.iloc[i, j]:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7) fig.colorbar(image, label="correlation") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-data_files/figure-html/02-5-run-1.png){width=1036.8} ::: ::: Thermal time and day length are almost collinear (0.97), since both increase through the year. Radiation and the maximum temperature follow the same yearly pattern (0.74 with day length, 0.66 between each other), `RAW` falls as the year progresses (−0.68 with day length), and `Tmin` and `VP` are strongly correlated (0.79). Rain is nearly uncorrelated with the other variables. Strongly correlated variables carry overlapping information, which is a first indication that a library does not need all eight. ## Response The response is the biomass (t/ha) of each genotype. Each panel is one year: all 199 genotypes in grey and three genotypes with the lowest, median and highest final biomass in colour. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} drv <- make_drivers(wx) tr <- make_trajectories(traj, drv) three <- spread_genotypes(tr) years <- traj[traj$year %in% c(1984, 1990, 1998, 2008), ] ggplot(years, aes(das, biomass, group = genotype)) + geom_line(colour = "#D1D5DB", linewidth = 0.2) + geom_line( data = years[years$genotype %in% three, ], aes(colour = genotype), linewidth = 0.7 ) + facet_wrap(~year, nrow = 1) + scale_colour_dgxe("burgundy", "cyan", "blue") + labs(x = "days after sowing", y = "biomass (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe() + legend_top() ``` ::: ## Python ```python drv = make_drivers(wx) tr = make_trajectories(traj, drv) three = spread_genotypes(tr) days = np.arange(tr.Y.shape[2]) + tr.das0 fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, sharey=True, figsize=(10, 2.8)) for ax, year in zip(axes, [1984, 1990, 1998, 2008]): s = list(tr.years).index(year) ax.plot(days, tr.Y[:, s].T, color=GREY, lw=0.2) for g, colour in zip(three, [BURGUNDY, CYAN, BLUE]): ax.plot(days, tr.Y[np.searchsorted(tr.genotypes, g), s], color=colour, lw=0.9, label=g) ax.set_title(year, loc="left") axes[0].legend(frameon=False) axes[0].set_ylabel("biomass (t/ha)") fig.supxlabel("days after sowing") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-data_files/figure-html/02-4-run-1.png){width=1036.8} ::: ::: Trajectories end on different days, since genotypes mature at different times. The array `tr$nend` records the length of each trajectory.
